Header: 2025-09-10 15:00 PDT — Duration 45m — Recording: yes — Meeting title: POC Weekly Sync - Throughput Optimization
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call? 
[00:05] Michael: Michael here, Michael Lopez, CTO. 
[00:07] Priya: Priya Sethi, ML Eng. 
[00:09] Daniel: Daniel Park, platform. 
[00:12] Samira: Samira Khan from Redwood, SE. Jordan's on AE. 
[00:18] Jordan: Awesome. Agenda: quick results review from last week's runs, tuning notes — continuous batching/concurrency/queueing — and plan next runs. We had Samira kick off a night run, Samira can start with results. 
[00:30] Samira: Sure. So the 3-hr steady-state on Thursday at our suggested concurrency target 16 showed average throughput of ~1,900 tok/s across the pod, with 95th latency at 220ms but 99th jumping to 780ms under short spikes. Logs attached in the shared folder: https://redwood.link/poc-atlas/throughput-20250904
[01:05] Priya: Okay 99th at 780ms is higher than our 500ms SLO. Where are the spikes coming from? 
[01:12] Samira: Mostly queue buildup when we had sudden inbound bursts above the target concurrency. The profiler shows several batches waiting in queue for 120-300ms before scheduling. Continuous batching improved overall token efficiency but introduced some head-of-line blocking when a very large request lands and dominates the batch window. 
[01:30] Daniel: That matches what we saw in production traces — a few big requests from billing that are long sequences and stall the GPU. We can't easily change request size upstream. 
[01:40] Samira: Right. Two levers we discussed: 1) enforce per-request max tokens or split long requests at the client (if possible); 2) adjust batching policy to prioritize latency-sensitive requests and cap batch size when queue depth exceeds threshold. We tested adaptive batch cap: when queue > 50ms wait, cap batch at 8 sequences, which reduced 99th latency to ~420ms but reduced token throughput by ~12%. 
[02:12] Michael: Tradeoff seems acceptable if 99th is under 500ms. But cost increase worries us. How much did cost/token change? 
[02:20] Samira: Roughly a 9% cost increase measured as tokens/core-hour because smaller batches lower utilization. But with autoscaling and cost-aware routing we can route very large requests to a lower-priority pool or model variant to avoid impacting critical paths. 
[02:35] Priya: Can we do KV cache warmups to reduce compute for repeated prefixes? A lot of requests share similar initial context. 
[02:42] Samira: Yes, prefix/KV caching is effective. We measured ~20% CPU/GPU reduction on warm paths. For your workload, enabling persistent KV cache on Dedicated instances gave best results; on Hosted it depends on session affinity. 
[02:58] Daniel: We're on sandbox Dedicated trial, right? Current pods are a mixed pool. For canary we'd prefer Dedicated. 
[03:05] Jordan: You have a small Dedicated trial — we've got two reserved workers for the POC. If we move to Dedicated for this route, we can pin KV cache and session affinity. Jordan: I'll surface pricing options after this call. 
[03:18] Priya: About concurrency targets — we ran with 16 earlier. Could we increase concurrency and rely on continuous batching to amortize overhead? 
[03:26] Samira: Increasing concurrency to 24 showed throughput up by 18% but tail latency worsened unless we also tuned the scheduler to preempt long requests. We tried token-aware preemption: if a request predicted >3k tokens, it goes to a separate queue. That fixed tail but required a separate worker pool for big requests. 
[03:52] Michael: How accurate is prediction of long requests? We don't want misclassification. 
[03:56] Samira: We use a light heuristic on Content-Length and a quick tokenizer pass to estimate. It was accurate about 92% on sample traces. Misclassifications were mostly shorter requests sent to big queue, which hurt throughput slightly. 
[04:12] Priya: Could we implement client-side hints — a header that says latency-sensitive vs best-effort? 
[04:16] Samira: Absolutely. We already support an x-redwood-priority header. If you can tag critical paths we can enforce strict scheduling for them. 
[04:24] Daniel: We'll need SDK changes in mobile and API gateway. That would take 1 sprint. 
[04:28] Jordan: Noted. Action item for Daniel team to prototype. 
[04:31] Speaker 1: (overlap) Also, there was a kernel flake last week... 
[04:34] Samira: Yeah, small aside — we saw a CUDA kernel stall on one worker during the 3:15 run, likely due to mixed-precision fallback on older GPU. We excluded that worker and re-ran which normalized results. For POC we recommend uniform GPU instance types. 
[04:52] Priya: Understood. About queueing — is there an out-of-the-box queue time SLA and alerting? 
[04:57] Samira: Console has queue-time dashboards and we can set alerts on the route: >200ms queue for 5m triggers paging. We can also add a synthetic test hitting critical route every minute. 
[05:09] Michael: Good. For next run, propose two experiments: A) adaptive batch cap with priority header, B) higher concurrency (24) with separate big-request pool. 
[05:18] Samira: We already prototyped both; A produced 99p < 500ms with 12% throughput loss, B produced 18% throughput gain but needed a big-request pool to keep 99p under SLO. 
[05:30] Priya: Which do you recommend for initial rollout? 
[05:33] Samira: Start with A — it's simpler and requires only scheduler changes and client hints. Then run B as a follow-up if you need more throughput. 
[05:40] Jordan: OK. Let's capture concrete next steps. Samira will share the updated dashboard link and runbook, run the A experiment in a 2-hour steady-state Tuesday 9/12. Priya/Daniel to add priority header in a canary gateway route. Jordan will send Dedicated pricing. 
[05:58] Michael: One last question on metrics — can we get token-level cost broken down per route in the console? 
[06:03] Samira: Yes, we can enable token-level billing for the POC account; we'll send the export as CSV. 
[06:12] Jordan: Great. Anything else? 
[06:15] Daniel: No, that's it. 
[06:17] Jordan: Thanks everyone. Recap and next steps will be emailed and I’ll set a follow-up for 9/17 canary test. 
[06:24] Michael: Thanks. 
Notes: Transcript has occasional mis-attributions and auto-capture errors; some timestamps approximate.
